text:
rami: FYI — onboarding tickets keep popping up. New users hit weird TS auto-imports that point to subpaths we removed when we cleaned exports.

zoe: Repro from user: clone examples/starter && npm i && node dist/server.js -> crashes with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM. They were using imports like `import { create } from '@redwood/sdk/client'`.

rami: Their package.json for the sdk currently has: "exports": {"./client": "./dist/client.cjs.js"}, "main": "dist/client.cjs.js" and `types` at top-level. We removed the import variant.

nate: Two problems: bundlers/TS pick up exports differently. Editors will auto-import the subpath if it exists in exports, but if it only points to CJS consumers doing `import` will fail.

zoe: Also saw a case where TS auto-import added `@redwood/sdk/client` while the published package only had types in `dist/index.d.ts` and not under the subpath, so intellisense lied.

rami: Example error from user: 
```
TypeError [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: Must use import to load ES Module: /home/user/project/node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/client.mjs
```

rami: They were on Node 16/18 and using Vite dev.

syl: Short fix: restore conditional subpath exports with explicit `import` + `require` + `types`. E.g.:
```json
"exports": {
  "./client": {
    "types": "./dist/client.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/client.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/client.cjs.js"
  }
}
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
```

nate: Also note pnpm workspace linking can hide this — local dev may still work because it imports from source, not published layout. Our CI didn't catch it for that reason.

zoe: We should add three things: 1) a small pack-install smoke test in examples that installs the tarball like a consumer; 2) a CI matrix: node require (16/18), node dynamic import (18+), vite dev build, esbuild bundle + `tsc --noEmit`; 3) a pre-publish lint that warns if exports subpaths lack both import and require.

dev-bot: CI: examples/pack-smoke -> exports-compat-matrix failed on step "node-import-check" (exit 1).

rami: I'll open a PR to add the conditional exports + types and wire the smoke job. Will include short onboarding note: "If you get ERR_REQUIRE_ESM or editor auto-imports the wrong subpath, check exports map and types mapping."

syl: Can we also add a tiny README snippet in examples showing both consume patterns so users can copy-paste: `const sdk = require('@redwood/sdk/client')` and `import sdk from '@redwood/sdk/client'`? Saves support time.

nate: Agreed. Also include a maintainer script: `scripts/pack-smoke.sh` that does `npm pack && npm init -w examples/starter && npm i ../sdk-*.tgz && npm run build && node -e "require('@redwood/sdk/client')" && node --input-type=module -e "import('@redwood/sdk/client')"` so CI can reuse it.

zoe: One more: add `./package.json` export mapping so bundlers can read package metadata from subpath imports if needed. E.g. "./package.json": "./package.json" in exports.

rami: Good note. I'll include that in the PR and a changelog line. Tagging @eng-platform for review.

dev-bot: PR 5135 opened by rami -> draft.
